    23→def enrich_with_impact(items: list[dict], dimension_scores: dict) -> None:
    24→    """Stamp ``estimated_impact`` on each item based on dimension-level headroom.
    25→
    26→    Impact = ``overall_per_point * headroom`` where headroom = ``100 - score``.
    27→    Items in dimensions with more score headroom sort first.
    28→    """
    29→    if not dimension_scores:
    30→        for item in items:
    31→            item["estimated_impact"] = 0.0
    32→        return
    33→
    34→    from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.health import compute_health_breakdown
    35→    from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.impact import get_dimension_for_detector
    36→
    37→    breakdown = compute_health_breakdown(dimension_scores)
    38→    entries = breakdown.get("entries", [])
    39→
    40→    # Build lookup: normalized dimension name -> {per_point, headroom}
    41→    dim_impact: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    42→    for entry in entries:
    43→        name = str(entry.get("name", "")).strip()
    44→        if not name:
    45→            continue
    46→        per_point = float(entry.get("overall_per_point", 0.0))
    47→        score = float(entry.get("score", 0.0))
    48→        headroom = 100.0 - score
    49→        dim_impact[name.lower()] = {"per_point": per_point, "headroom": headroom}
    50→
    51→    for item in items:
    52→        impact = _compute_item_impact(item, dim_impact, get_dimension_for_detector)
    53→        item["estimated_impact"] = impact
    54→
    55→
    56→def _compute_item_impact(
    57→    item: dict,
    58→    dim_impact: dict[str, dict[str, float]],
    59→    get_dimension_for_detector,
    60→) -> float:
    61→    """Compute impact value for a single queue item."""
    62→    kind = item.get("kind", "finding")
    63→
    64→    # Subjective items (synthetic dimensions or subjective findings):
    65→    # look up by detail.dimension_name
    66→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
    67→        dim_name = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    68→        entry = dim_impact.get(dim_name.lower())
    69→        if entry:
    70→            return entry["per_point"] * entry["headroom"]
    71→        return 0.0
    72→
    73→    # Mechanical findings: use detector -> dimension mapping
    74→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    75→    if detector:
    76→        dimension = get_dimension_for_detector(detector)
    77→        if dimension:
    78→            entry = dim_impact.get(dimension.name.lower())
    79→            if entry:
    80→                return entry["per_point"] * entry["headroom"]
    81→
    82→    return 0.0
    83→
    84→
    85→def subjective_score_value(item: dict) -> float:
    86→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    87→        detail = detail_dict(item)
    88→        return float(detail.get("strict_score", item.get("subjective_score", 100.0)))
    89→    return float(item.get("subjective_score", 100.0))
    90→
    91→
    92→def build_finding_items(
    93→    state: dict,
    94→    *,
    95→    scan_path: str | None,
    96→    status_filter: str,
    97→    scope: str | None,
    98→    chronic: bool,
    99→) -> list[dict]:
   100→    scoped = path_scoped_findings(state.get("findings", {}), scan_path)
   101→    subjective_scores = subjective_strict_scores(state)
   102→    out: list[dict] = []
   103→
   104→    for finding_id, finding in scoped.items():
   105→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
   106→            continue
   107→        if not status_matches(finding.get("status", "open"), status_filter):
   108→            continue
   109→        if chronic and not (
   110→            finding.get("status") == "open" and finding.get("reopen_count", 0) >= 2
   111→        ):
   112→            continue
   113→
   114→        # Evidence-only: skip findings below standalone confidence threshold
   115→        detector = finding.get("detector", "")
   116→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   117→        if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
   118→            threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
   119→            finding_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(finding.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
   120→            if finding_rank > threshold_rank:
   121→                continue
   122→
   123→        item = dict(finding)
   124→        item["id"] = finding_id
   125→        item["kind"] = "finding"
   126→        item["is_review"] = is_review_finding(item)
   127→        item["is_subjective"] = is_subjective_finding(item)
   128→        item["review_weight"] = (
   129→            review_finding_weight(item) if item["is_review"] else None
   130→        )
   131→        subjective_score = None
   132→        if item["is_subjective"]:
   133→            detail = detail_dict(finding)
   134→            dim_name = detail.get("dimension_name", "")
   135→            dim_key = detail.get("dimension", "") or slugify(dim_name)
   136→            subjective_score = subjective_scores.get(
   137→                dim_key, subjective_scores.get(dim_name.lower(), 100.0)
   138→            )
   139→        item["subjective_score"] = subjective_score
   140→        supported_fixers = supported_fixers_for_item(state, item)
   141→        item["primary_command"] = primary_command_for_finding(
   142→            item,
   143→            supported_fixers=supported_fixers,
   144→        )
   145→
   146→        if not scope_matches(item, scope):
   147→            continue
   148→        out.append(item)
   149→
   150→    return out
   151→
   152→
   153→def item_sort_key(item: dict) -> tuple:
   154→    kind = item.get("kind", "finding")
   155→
   156→    # Initial-review subjective items: highest priority (tier -3)
   157→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" and item.get("initial_review"):
   158→        return (-3, 0, subjective_score_value(item), item.get("id", ""))
   159→
   160→    # Triage stage items: tier -2, stage order, blocked after unblocked
   161→    if kind == "workflow_stage":
   162→        blocked_penalty = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   163→        stage_index = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   164→        return (-2, blocked_penalty, stage_index, item.get("id", ""))
   165→
   166→    # Workflow action items (e.g. create-plan): tier -1
   167→    if kind == "workflow_action":
   168→        return (-1, 0, 0, item.get("id", ""))
   169→
   170→    if kind == "cluster":
   171→        # Clusters sort before individual findings, ordered by action type
   172→        action_pri = ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY.get(
   173→            item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"), 3
   174→        )
   175→        return (
   176→            0,
   177→            action_pri,
   178→            -int(item.get("member_count", 0)),
   179→            item.get("id", ""),
   180→        )
   181→
   182→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0)
   183→
   184→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
   185→        return (
   186→            1,
   187→            -impact,
   188→            subjective_score_value(item),
   189→            item.get("id", ""),
   190→        )
   191→
   192→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   193→    review_weight = float(item.get("review_weight", 0.0) or 0.0)
   194→    return (
   195→        1,
   196→        -impact,
   197→        CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(item.get("confidence", "low"), 9),
   198→        -review_weight,
   199→        -int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   200→        item.get("id", ""),
   201→    )
   202→
   203→
   204→def item_explain(item: dict) -> dict:
   205→    kind = item.get("kind", "finding")

   211→            "blocked_by": item.get("blocked_by", []),

   215→
   216→    if kind == "workflow_action":

   223→    if kind == "cluster":

   227→            "action_type": item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"),
   228→            "member_count": item.get("member_count", 0),
   229→            "policy": "Clusters sort before individual findings, ordered by action type then size.",
   230→            "ranking_factors": ["action_type asc", "member_count desc", "id asc"],

   405→        open_review = sum(review_open_by_dim.get(alias, 0) for alias in aliases)

   413→        if open_review > 0:

   415→        else:

    19→def supported_fixers(state: StateModel, lang: str | None) -> set[str] | None:
    20→    """Return supported fixers for the active language, or None when unknown."""
    21→    if not lang:
    22→        return None
    23→
    24→    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities", {}).get(lang, {})
    25→    fixers = capabilities.get("fixers")
    26→    if isinstance(fixers, list):
    27→        return {fixer for fixer in fixers if isinstance(fixer, str)}
    28→
    29→    try:
    30→        return set(get_lang(lang).fixers.keys())
    31→    except (ImportError, ValueError):
    32→        return None

    35→def _impact_calculator(
    36→    dimension_scores: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    37→    state: StateModel,
    38→) -> Callable[[str, int], float]:
    39→    """Build an impact estimator closure keyed by detector and count."""
    40→    merged_potentials = merge_potentials(state.get("potentials", {}))
    41→    if not merged_potentials or not dimension_scores:
    42→        return lambda _detector, _count: 0.0
    43→
    44→    scoring_view = {
    45→        name: {
    46→            "score": values["score"],
    47→            "tier": values.get("tier", 3),
    48→            "detectors": values.get("detectors", {}),
    49→        }
    50→        for name, values in dimension_scores.items()
    51→    }
    52→
    53→    def _impact(detector: str, count: int) -> float:
    54→        return compute_score_impact(
    55→            scoring_view, merged_potentials, detector, count
    56→        )
    57→
    58→    return _impact

    61→def _dimension_name(detector: str) -> str:
    62→    """Resolve user-facing dimension name for a detector."""
    63→    dimension = get_dimension_for_detector(detector)
    64→    return dimension.name if dimension else "Unknown"
    65→
    66→
    67→def _fixer_has_applicable_findings(
    68→    state: StateModel, detector: str, fixer_name: str
    69→) -> bool:
    70→    """For the smells detector, verify the fixer has matching open findings.
    71→
    72→    The smells detector aggregates many smell types but each fixer only handles
    73→    one sub-type (e.g. ``dead-useeffect`` only fixes ``dead_useeffect`` smells).
    74→    Without this check, a React-specific fixer can be suggested to projects that
    75→    have no React code at all, producing a confusing "Found 0 candidates" result.
    76→
    77→    For all other detectors the fixer is considered universally applicable.
    78→    """
    79→    if detector != "smells":
    80→        return True
    81→    smell_id = fixer_name.replace("-", "_")
    82→    return any(
    83→        f.get("status") == "open"
    84→        and not f.get("suppressed")
    85→        and f.get("detector") == "smells"
    86→        and f.get("detail", {}).get("smell_id") == smell_id
    87→        for f in state.get("findings", {}).values()
    88→    )
    89→

    91→def _append_auto_fix_actions(
    92→    actions: list[ActionItem],

    94→    supported: set[str] | None,
    95→    impact_for: Callable[[str, int], float],
    96→    state: StateModel,
    97→) -> None:
    98→    """Append auto-fix/manual-fix actions for detectors with auto fixers."""
    99→    for detector, tool_info in DETECTOR_TOOLS.items():

   123→                    "command": f"desloppify show {detector} --status open",
   124→                    "impact": impact,

     2→
     3→Shared utilities (string-aware scanning, brace tracking, comment stripping)
     4→plus a handful of smell detectors. Monster-function, dead-function,
     5→window-global, catch-return-default, and switch-no-default detectors live

    28→    track_brace_body as _track_brace_body_impl,
    29→)
    30→
    31→
    32→def _strip_ts_comments(text: str) -> str:
    33→    """Strip // and /* */ comments while preserving strings.
    34→
    35→    Delegates to the shared implementation in utils.py.
    36→    """
    37→    return strip_c_style_comments(text)
    38→
    39→
    40→def _ts_match_is_in_string(line: str, match_start: int) -> bool:
    41→    """Check if a match position falls inside a string literal or comment on a single line.
    42→
    43→    Mirrors Python's _match_is_in_string but for TS syntax (', ", `, //).
    44→    """
    45→    i = 0
    46→    in_str = None
    47→
    48→    while i < len(line):
    49→        if i == match_start:
    50→            return in_str is not None
    51→
    52→        ch = line[i]
    53→
    54→        # Escape sequences inside strings
    55→        if in_str and ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(line):
    56→            i += 2
    57→            continue
    58→
    59→        if in_str:
    60→            if ch == in_str:
    61→                in_str = None
    62→            i += 1
    63→            continue
    64→
    65→        # Line comment — everything after is non-code
    66→        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(line) and line[i + 1] == "/":
    67→            return match_start > i
    68→
    69→        if ch in ("'", '"', "`"):
    70→            in_str = ch
    71→            i += 1
    72→            continue
    73→
    74→        i += 1
    75→
    76→    return False
    77→
    78→
    79→def _detect_async_no_await(
    80→    filepath: str, content: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
    81→):
    82→    """Find async functions that don't use await.
    83→
    84→    Algorithm: for each async declaration, track brace depth to find the function
    85→    body extent (up to 200 lines). Scan each line for 'await' within those braces.
    86→    If the opening brace closes (depth returns to 0) without seeing await, flag it.
    87→    """
    88→    async_re = re.compile(r"(?:async\s+function\s+(\w+)|(\w+)\s*=\s*async)")
    89→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    90→        m = async_re.search(line)
    91→        if not m:
    92→            continue
    93→        name = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
    94→        brace_depth = 0
    95→        found_open = False
    96→        has_await = False
    97→        for j in range(i, min(i + 200, len(lines))):
    98→            body_line = lines[j]
    99→            prev_code_ch = ""
   100→            for _, ch, in_s in scan_code(body_line):
   101→                if in_s:
   102→                    continue
   103→                if ch == "/" and prev_code_ch == "/":
   104→                    break  # Rest of line is comment
   105→                elif ch == "{":
   106→                    brace_depth += 1
   107→                    found_open = True
   108→                elif ch == "}":
   109→                    brace_depth -= 1
   110→                prev_code_ch = ch
   111→            if "await " in body_line or "await\n" in body_line:
   112→                has_await = True
   113→            if found_open and brace_depth <= 0:
   114→                break
   115→
   116→        if found_open and not has_await:
   117→            smell_counts["async_no_await"].append(
   118→                {
   119→                    "file": filepath,
   120→                    "line": i + 1,
   121→                    "content": f"async {name or '(anonymous)'} has no await",
   122→                }
   123→            )
   124→
   125→
   126→def _detect_error_no_throw(
   127→    filepath: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   128→):
   129→    """Find console.error calls not followed by throw or return."""
   130→    _detect_error_no_throw_impl(filepath, lines, smell_counts)
   131→
   132→
   133→def _detect_empty_if_chains(
   134→    filepath: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   135→):
   136→    """Find if/else chains where all branches are empty."""
   137→    _detect_empty_if_chains_impl(filepath, lines, smell_counts)
   138→
   139→
   140→def _detect_dead_useeffects(
   141→    filepath: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   142→):
   143→    """Find useEffect calls with empty or whitespace/comment-only bodies.
   144→
   145→    Algorithm: two-pass brace/paren tracking with string-escape awareness.
   146→    Pass 1: track paren depth to find the full useEffect(...) extent.
   147→    Pass 2: within that extent, find the arrow body ({...} after =>) using
   148→    brace depth, skipping characters inside string literals (', ", `).
   149→    Then strip comments from the body and check if anything remains.
   150→    """
   151→    _detect_dead_useeffects_impl(
   152→        filepath,
   153→        lines,
   154→        smell_counts,
   155→        scan_code_fn=scan_code,
   156→        strip_ts_comments_fn=_strip_ts_comments,
   157→    )
   158→
   159→
   160→def _detect_swallowed_errors(
   161→    filepath: str, content: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   162→):
   163→    """Find catch blocks whose only content is console.error/warn/log (swallowed errors).
   164→
   165→    Algorithm: regex-find each `catch(...) {`, then track brace depth with
   166→    string-escape awareness to extract the catch body (up to 500 chars).
   167→    Strip comments, split into statements, and check if every statement
   168→    is a console.error/warn/log call.
   169→    """
   170→    _detect_swallowed_errors_impl(
   171→        filepath,
   172→        content,
   173→        lines,
   174→        smell_counts,
   175→        scan_code_fn=scan_code,
   176→        strip_ts_comments_fn=_strip_ts_comments,
   177→    )
   178→
   179→
   180→def _track_brace_body(
   181→    lines: list[str], start_line: int, *, max_scan: int = 2000
   182→) -> int | None:
   183→    """Find the closing brace that matches the first opening brace from start_line.
   184→
   185→    Tracks brace depth with string-literal awareness (', ", `).
   186→    Returns the line index of the closing brace, or None if not found.
   187→    """
   188→    return _track_brace_body_impl(
   189→        lines,
   190→        start_line,
   191→        scan_code_fn=scan_code,
   192→        max_scan=max_scan,
   193→    )

    95→# Detectors where potential = file count but findings are per-(file, sub-type).

   102→
   103→
   104→def _build_dimensions() -> list[Dimension]:
   105→    """Derive dimensions from DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES.
   106→
   107→    Each unique (dimension, tier) pair becomes a Dimension, with its detectors
   108→    collected automatically. Order follows first-seen in the policies dict.
   109→    """
   110→    # Collect (dimension_name -> tier) preserving first-seen order,
   111→    # and group detectors by dimension.
   112→    dim_tiers: dict[str, int] = {}
   113→    grouped: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   114→    for detector, policy in DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES.items():
   115→        if policy.dimension is None or policy.tier is None:
   116→            continue
   117→        if policy.dimension not in dim_tiers:
   118→            dim_tiers[policy.dimension] = policy.tier
   119→            grouped[policy.dimension] = []
   120→        grouped[policy.dimension].append(detector)
   121→    return [
   122→        Dimension(name=name, tier=tier, detectors=grouped[name])
   123→        for name, tier in dim_tiers.items()
   124→    ]
   125→
   126→
   127→DIMENSIONS = _build_dimensions()
   128→DIMENSIONS_BY_NAME = {d.name: d for d in DIMENSIONS}
   129→
   130→TIER_WEIGHTS = {
   131→    Tier.AUTO_FIX: 1,
   132→    Tier.QUICK_FIX: 2,
   133→    Tier.JUDGMENT: 3,
   134→    Tier.MAJOR_REFACTOR: 4,
   135→}
   136→CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTS = {Confidence.HIGH: 1.0, Confidence.MEDIUM: 0.7, Confidence.LOW: 0.3}
   137→
   138→# Minimum checks for full dimension weight — below this, weight is dampened
   139→# proportionally. Prevents small-sample dimensions from swinging the overall score.
   140→MIN_SAMPLE = 200
   141→
   142→# Holistic review weight: findings with file="." and detail.holistic=True
   143→# get a 10x weight multiplier for display/priority purposes (issues list,
   144→# remediation engine).  NOT used in score computation — review findings are
   145→# excluded from the detection scoring pipeline (scored via assessments only).
   146→HOLISTIC_MULTIPLIER = 10.0
   147→HOLISTIC_POTENTIAL = 10
   148→
   149→# Budget: subjective dimensions get this fraction of the overall score.
   150→# Mechanical dimensions get the remainder.
   151→SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION = 0.60
   152→MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION = 1.0 - SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   153→
   154→# Per-dimension weighting within the mechanical pool.
   155→# Keep this balanced: no special boost for security/test in the pool itself.
   156→MECHANICAL_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS: dict[str, float] = {
   157→    "file health": 2.0,
   158→    "code quality": 1.0,
   159→    "duplication": 1.0,
   160→    "test health": 1.0,
   161→    "security": 1.0,
   162→}
   163→
   164→# Per-dimension weighting within the subjective pool.
   165→# Emphasize elegance and contract/type coherence for a stronger architecture north star.
   166→SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS: dict[str, float] = {
   167→    "high elegance": 22.0,
   168→    "mid elegance": 22.0,
   169→    "low elegance": 12.0,
   170→    "contracts": 12.0,
   171→    "type safety": 12.0,
   172→    "abstraction fit": 8.0,
   173→    "logic clarity": 6.0,
   174→    # Low-but-meaningful structural signal (about half of the subjective
   175→    # average weight) so it matters without dominating craftsmanship axes.
   176→    "structure nav": 5.0,
   177→    "error consistency": 3.0,
   178→    "naming quality": 2.0,
   179→    "ai generated debt": 1.0,
   180→    "design coherence": 10.0,
   181→}
   182→
   183→# Synthetic check count for subjective dimensions in dimension_scores.
   184→SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS = 10
   185→
   186→FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE: dict[ScoreMode, frozenset[str]] = {
   187→    "lenient": frozenset({"open"}),
   188→    "strict": frozenset({"open", "wontfix"}),
   189→    "verified_strict": frozenset({"open", "wontfix", "fixed", "false_positive"}),
   190→}
   191→
   192→# Tolerance for treating a subjective score as "on target" in integrity checks.
   193→# Scores within this band of the target are flagged as potential gaming.
   194→SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_MATCH_TOLERANCE = 0.05
   195→
   196→
   197→def matches_target_score(
   198→    score: object,
   199→    target: object,
   200→    *,
   201→    tolerance: float = SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_MATCH_TOLERANCE,
   202→) -> bool:
   203→    """Return True when score is within tolerance of target."""
   204→    try:
   205→        score_value = float(score)
   206→        target_value = float(target)
   207→        tolerance_value = max(0.0, float(tolerance))
   208→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   209→        return False
   210→    return abs(score_value - target_value) <= tolerance_value
   211→
   212→
   213→def register_scoring_policy(policy: DetectorScoringPolicy) -> None:
   214→    """Register a scoring policy at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   215→    DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES[policy.detector] = policy
   216→    _rebuild_derived()
   217→
   218→
   219→def reset_registered_scoring_policies() -> None:
   220→    """Reset runtime-added scoring policies to built-in defaults."""
   221→    DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES.clear()
   222→    DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES.update(_BASE_DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES)
   223→    _rebuild_derived()
   224→
   225→
   226→def _rebuild_derived() -> None:
   227→    """Rebuild DIMENSIONS, DIMENSIONS_BY_NAME, FILE_BASED_DETECTORS from current state.
   228→
   229→    Mutates existing objects in-place so that all references (including imports
   230→    that bound the original objects) see the updates.
   231→    """
   232→    new_dims = _build_dimensions()
   233→    DIMENSIONS.clear()
   234→    DIMENSIONS.extend(new_dims)
   235→    DIMENSIONS_BY_NAME.clear()
   236→    DIMENSIONS_BY_NAME.update({d.name: d for d in DIMENSIONS})
   237→    FILE_BASED_DETECTORS.clear()
   238→    FILE_BASED_DETECTORS.update(
   239→        det for det, pol in DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES.items() if pol.file_based
   240→    )
   241→
   242→
   243→def detector_policy(detector: str) -> DetectorScoringPolicy:
   244→    """Get scoring policy for a detector, with a safe default fallback."""
   245→    return DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES.get(
   246→        detector,
   247→        DetectorScoringPolicy(detector=detector, dimension=None, tier=None),
   248→    )
   249→
   250→

## Comprehensive Analysis: TypeScript Smell Detection System

### 1. **Main Smell Detection Flow** (`smells.py`)

The `detect_smells(path: Path)` function (lines 553-643) is the entry point. It:
- Collects all TypeScript files via `find_ts_files(path)`
- For each file:
  - Reads the content and splits into lines
  - Builds line state map via `_build_ts_line_state()` (tracks block comments and template literals)
  - Applies regex-based checks for simple smells
  - Calls multi-line helper functions for complex smells
- Returns `(entries, total_files_checked)` where entries are grouped by smell ID with severity

**Key finding structure from regex matches:**
```python
{
    "file": filepath,
    "line": i + 1,
    "content": line.strip()[:100],
}
```

### 2. **TS_SMELL_CHECKS Registry** (lines 35-218)

A 32-item registry of all smell patterns with metadata:
```python
{
    "id": string (detector ID),
    "label": string (human-readable name),
    "pattern": regex string OR None (for multi-line analysis),
    "severity": "high" | "medium" | "low",
}
```

**Severity breakdown:**
- **High (tier 2/QUICK_FIX):** empty_catch, ts_nocheck, empty_if_chain, dead_useeffect, monster_function, catch_return_default
- **Medium (tier 3/JUDGMENT):** any_type, ts_ignore, hardcoded colors/RGB/URLs, async_no_await, console_error_no_throw, swallowed_error, dead_function, window_global, as_any_cast, sort_no_comparator, nested_closure, high_cyclomatic_complexity
- **Low (tier 3/JUDGMENT):** non_null_assert, magic_number, todo_fixme, debug_tag, voided_symbol, workaround_tag, switch_no_default, css_monolith, css_important_overuse, docs_scripts_drift

### 3. **Line State Building** (`_build_ts_line_state()`, lines 221-341)

Preprocesses source to identify which lines are inside:
- **Block comments** (`/* ... */`)
- **Template literals** (backtick strings with `${}` nesting awareness)

Returns `{line_index: reason}` map. Lines not in map are safe for regex checks. This prevents false positives in comments/strings.

**Handles:**
- Escape sequences (`\.`)
- Template `${}` nesting depth tracking
- Block comment closing detection

### 4. **Multi-line Smell Helpers** (`_smell_helpers.py`)

All delegate to implementations in `_smell_effects.py` and use the `scan_code()` function.

**Key functions:**
- `_detect_async_no_await()` - Finds async functions without await using brace depth tracking
- `_detect_error_no_throw()` - Finds console.error without throw/return in next 3 lines
- `_detect_empty_if_chains()` - Regex-based single-line detection
- `_detect_dead_useeffects()` - Uses brace and paren tracking
- `_detect_swallowed_errors()` - Find catch blocks with only console calls
- `_track_brace_body()` - Helper to find closing brace matching first opening brace

### 5. **scan_code() Function** (`desloppify/languages/typescript/syntax/scanner.py`, lines 8-34)

**Critical utility generator:**
```python
def scan_code(
    text: str, start: int = 0, end: int | None = None
) -> Generator[tuple[int, str, bool], None, None]:
    """Yield (index, char, in_string) tuples with escape-aware string tracking."""
```

**Key behavior:**
- Tracks when cursor is inside string literals (`'`, `"`, backticks)
- Yields `(character_index, character, is_inside_string_literal)` tuples
- Handles escape sequences (`\\`) — both escape char and next char marked as `in_string=True`
- Used by all multi-line detectors to skip string/comment content

**Critical detail:** String delimiters themselves are marked `in_string=True` after entering, `in_string=False` after exiting (line 26).

### 6. **Multi-line Smell Effects** (`_smell_effects.py`)

Implements actual detection logic:

**`detect_error_no_throw()`** (lines 8-24)
- Simple: finds `console.error` then checks next 3 lines for `throw`/`return`
- No string awareness

**`detect_empty_if_chains()`** (lines 27-106)
- Regex-based detection of `if(){} else if(){} else {}`
- Two patterns: single-line `{ }` and multi-line tracking

**`detect_dead_useeffects()`** (lines 109-174)
- Paren tracking to find full `useEffect(...)`
- Then brace tracking to find arrow body `{...}` after `=>`
- Strips comments and checks if body is empty
- **Uses `scan_code_fn` callbacks** for string awareness

**`detect_swallowed_errors()`** (lines 177-236)
- Regex-find `catch(...) {`
- Brace depth tracking (max 500 chars)
- Checks if body is **only** console.error/warn/log calls
- Uses `scan_code_fn` for string awareness

**`track_brace_body()`** (lines 239-260)
- Generic brace-depth tracker
- Returns closing brace line index
- Uses `scan_code_fn` for string awareness

### 7. **Multi-line Smell Detectors** (`_smell_detectors.py`)

**`_detect_monster_functions()`** (lines 72-99)
- Uses `_find_function_start()` to identify function declarations and named arrow functions
- Uses `_track_brace_body()` to find closing brace
- Flags if LOC > 150
- Skips decorated functions, interfaces, types, enums

**`_detect_dead_functions()`** (lines 102-150)
- Identifies functions via `_find_function_start()`
- Extracts body between braces
- Strips comments with `_strip_ts_comments()`
- Flags if body is: `""`, `"return"`, `"return null"`, `"return undefined"`
- **Skips functions with decorators** (line 112)

**`_detect_window_globals()`** (lines 153-187)
- Regex patterns for `window.__*`, `(window as any).__*`, `window['__*']`
- Checks for `=` assignment

**`_detect_catch_return_default()`** (lines 190-267)
- Finds `catch(...) { return { ... } }`
- Counts "default" fields: `false`, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, `''`, `""`, `() => {}`
- Flags if 2+ default fields

**`_detect_switch_no_default()`** (lines 381-428)
- Finds switch with no `default:` case
- Only flags if 2+ cases exist

**`_detect_nested_closures()`** (lines 308-332)
- Counts nested `function` and `=>` declarations in function body
- Flags if 3+ nested closures

**`_detect_high_cyclomatic_complexity()`** (lines 357-378)
- Uses `_compute_ts_cyclomatic_complexity()` to count branches
- Flags if complexity > 15

### 8. **Helper Functions**

**`_find_function_start(line, next_lines)`** (lines 30-63)
- Returns function name for:
  - Declaration: `function foo()`
  - Assignment: `const/let/var foo = ...`
  - Arrow: `const foo = (...) => {`
- Returns None for: interfaces, types, enums, non-function assignments

**`_strip_ts_comments(text)`** (lines 32-37 in _smell_helpers.py)
- Delegates to `strip_c_style_comments()` from `desloppify.core.text_api`
- Removes `//` and `/* */` while preserving strings

**`_ts_match_is_in_string(line, match_start)`** (lines 40-76 in _smell_helpers.py)
- Checks if a regex match position falls inside a string (`'`, `"`, backtick) or comment on single line
- Iterates left-to-right tracking string state

### 9. **Confidence Assignment**

**In `make_smell_findings()` (finding_factories.py, lines 192-223):**
```python
conf = "medium" if e["severity"] != "low" else "low"
tier = SMELL_TIER_MAP.get(e["severity"], 3)
```

**Rules:**
- **High severity** → confidence="medium", tier=2 (QUICK_FIX)
- **Medium severity** → confidence="medium", tier=3 (JUDGMENT)
- **Low severity** → confidence="low", tier=3 (JUDGMENT)

All findings are created via `make_finding()` with the tier and confidence from above.

### 10. **Exclusion Mechanisms**

**Current exclusions in smell detection:**
1. **File-level:** Skips `node_modules/*` and `*.d.ts` files (line 563 in smells.py)
2. **Line state filtering:** Skips lines in block comments/template literals (line 588)
3. **String/comment detection:** `_ts_match_is_in_string()` filters regex matches in strings/comments (line 594)
4. **Hardcoded URL exception:** Skips URLs assigned to module-level constants (lines 597-601)
5. **Function decorator skip:** Dead/monster function detectors skip `@decorated` functions (line 112 in _smell_detectors.py)

**NO general exclusion mechanism** like the memory describes (`matches_exclusion()`, `_extra_exclusions`) is currently applied in smell detection. This is available in `discovery_api.py` but not used by the smell detection pipeline.

**`matches_exclusion(rel_path, exclusion)`** exists in `core/file_paths.py` (lines 13-32) and supports:
- Component matching: `"node_modules" in path_parts`
- Glob patterns: `fnmatch` on path parts
- Full-path globs: `"dir/**"` style patterns

### Summary

The TS smell detection system is **comprehensive and modular**:
- **Regex-based** smells for simple patterns (strings, comments safe-guarded)
- **Multi-line analysis** with **string-aware character scanning** (via `scan_code()`)
- **Brace/paren depth tracking** for function boundaries and block extraction
- **Three-tier confidence** based on smell severity (high=medium conf, low=low conf)
- **Limited exclusion** (file/line state/string filtering only, no config-based exclusions)

All files and code are now fully understood and ready for modification planning.

## Comprehensive Report: Subjective Review System in Desloppify

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's how the subjective review system works:

---

### 1. **Classification: Subjective vs Objective Findings**

**Objective (Mechanical) Findings:**
- Findings from detectors with clear-cut, deterministic logic
- Examples: `unused`, `logs`, `exports`, `deprecated`, `security`
- Can be auto-fixed or manually reviewed without judgment calls
- Come from most detectors in the registry

**Subjective (Non-Objective) Findings:**
- Findings that require human judgment and design evaluation
- Detector list defined in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/subjective_policy.py` (lines 16-18):
  ```python
  NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
      "review", "concerns", "subjective_review", "subjective_assessment",
  })
  ```
- These detectors are **never counted toward the objective backlog** and are gated by visibility policy
- Synthetic items created by `build_subjective_items()` for dimension assessments

---

### 2. **Confidence Levels and Evidence-Only Filtering**

**Confidence Enum** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/core/enums.py`):
```python
class Confidence(enum.StrEnum):
    HIGH = "high"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    LOW = "low"
```

**Evidence-Only Filtering** (NEW in v0.9.0):
- Registry field `standalone_threshold: str | None` on `DetectorMeta` specifies minimum confidence for a finding to appear as a standalone queue item
- Detectors with `standalone_threshold="medium"`: `smells`, `naming`, `props`, `react`, `dupes`, `patterns`, `dict_keys` (lines 93, 130, 184, 193, 202, 211, 221 in registry.py)
- **Key logic** in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/subjective_policy.py` (lines 64-76):
  ```python
  def _is_evidence_only(finding: dict) -> bool:
      """Return True if the finding is below its detector's standalone threshold."""
      detector = finding.get("detector", "")
      meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
      if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
          threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
          finding_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(finding.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
          if finding_rank > threshold_rank:  # "low"=2 > "medium"=1
              return True
      return False
  ```
- **Evidence-only findings:**
  - Remain in state and contribute to dimension scores
  - Are **filtered out from work queue** (not surfaced as standalone items)
  - Still affect subjective visibility policy
  - Useful for review evidence without forcing immediate action

---

### 3. **Review Flow Architecture**

**Subjective Review Command** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/fix/review_flow.py`):
1. User runs `desloppify autofix review --prepare`
2. `_cmd_fix_review()` function:
   - Loads state and resolves language config
   - Calls `review_mod.prepare_review()` to gather files needing design review
   - Writes dimension prompts to `.desloppify/query.json`
   - Prints multi-step agent plan for reviewers (local Codex, Claude cloud durable, or findings-only)

**Three Review Paths:**
1. **Codex (local)**: `desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import`
2. **Claude cloud durable**: `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude` (then submit results)
3. **Findings-only fallback**: Manual `desloppify review --import findings.json && desloppify scan`

---

### 4. **Detector Routing: Auto-Fix vs Subjective Review**

**Auto-Fix Detectors** (`action_type="auto_fix"`):
- Examples: `unused`, `logs`
- Have fixers in their config
- Can be applied without human judgment
- Routed to `desloppify autofix <fixer-name>` flow

**Refactor/Judgment Detectors** (`needs_judgment=True`):
- Examples: `orphaned`, `uncalled_functions`, `naming`, `coupling`, `patterns`, `props`, `react`
- Require design judgment but focus on code structure
- Suggested for `desloppify show <detector> --status open` inspection
- May have `standalone_threshold` to filter low-confidence variants

**Subjective Assessment Detectors**:
- `subjective_assessment`: Synthetic dimension items created during queue building
- `review`: AI code review findings (from previous review runs)
- `subjective_review`: Trigger for dimension refresh via `desloppify review --prepare`
- `holistic_review`: Special review findings marked as holistic in detail

**Key Distinction in Queue Building** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/ranking.py`, lines 114-121):
```python
# Evidence-only: skip findings below standalone confidence threshold
detector = finding.get("detector", "")
meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
    threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
    finding_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(finding.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
    if finding_rank > threshold_rank:
        continue  # Skip from queue
```

---

### 5. **Subjective Visibility Policy**

**Core Data Structure** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/subjective_policy.py`):
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SubjectiveVisibility:
    has_objective_backlog: bool      # any open non-subjective findings?
    objective_count: int             # count excluding evidence-only
    unscored_ids: frozenset[str]     # subjective::* IDs needing initial review
    stale_ids: frozenset[str]        # subjective::* IDs needing re-review
    under_target_ids: frozenset[str] # below target, not stale/unscored
```

**Visibility Rules** (`compute_subjective_visibility()`, lines 79-119):
1. Count objective findings:
   - Open status
   - NOT in `NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS`
   - Not suppressed
   - **NOT evidence-only** (per `_is_evidence_only()`)
2. Compute three subjective dimension categories:
   - **Unscored (initial_review)**: Placeholder assessments needing first evaluation
   - **Stale**: Assessments flagged `needs_review_refresh=True`
   - **Under target**: Strict scores < 95% and not stale

**Surfacing Logic** (`should_surface()`, lines 31-38):
```python
def should_surface(self, item: dict) -> bool:
    """Unscored (initial_review) -> always. All others -> only when drained."""
    if item.get("initial_review"):
        return True  # Always surface unscored dimensions
    return not self.has_objective_backlog  # Surface other subjective only when objective work is done
```

---

### 6. **Work Queue Ordering and Priority**

**Item Sort Order** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/ranking.py`, lines 153-200):
1. **Tier -3**: Initial-review subjective dimensions (unscored)
2. **Tier -2**: Workflow/triage stage items (blocked after unblocked)
3. **Tier -1**: Workflow action items (e.g., create-plan)
4. **Tier 0**: Clusters (sorted by action type priority)
5. **Tier 1**: All other items (mechanical findings, stale subjective, under-target subjective)
   - Sorted by: estimated impact (descending), confidence, review weight, count

**Build Work Queue** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py`, lines 64-157):
1. Build finding items (excludes evidence-only)
2. Compute subjective visibility policy
3. Build subjective dimension items (`build_subjective_items()`)
4. Gate subjective items: only surface if `policy.should_surface(item)` or explicitly in plan
5. Filter by impact floor: drop mechanical findings with `estimated_impact < 0.05`
6. Apply plan ordering if provided
7. Return ranked queue

---

### 7. **How Subjective Dimensions Are Created**

**Synthetic Subjective Items** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py`, lines 346-441):
- Created for each dimension in `dimension_scores` with `subjective_entries`
- Generated **per call** during queue building (not stored)
- Each item has:
  - `id`: `subjective::{slugify(dimension_key)}`
  - `detector`: `subjective_assessment`
  - `kind`: `subjective_dimension`
  - `initial_review`: True if unassessed or placeholder
  - `stale_review`: True if flagged for refresh
  - `subjective_score`: Strict score from dimension_scores
  - `primary_command`: `desloppify review --prepare` or `desloppify show review`

---

### 8. **Impact Floor and Negligible-Impact Filtering**

**Minimum Standalone Impact** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py`, lines 135-144):
```python
MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT = 0.05
all_items = [
    item for item in all_items
    if item.get("kind") != "finding"
    or item.get("is_review")
    or item.get("is_subjective")
    or not item.get("estimated_impact")
    or item["estimated_impact"] >= MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT
]
```
- Mechanical findings with negligible score impact are dropped even if confidence is high
- `is_review` and `is_subjective` items always included (not subject to impact floor)
- Reason: Fixing 1 finding in a dimension at 99.99% score has near-zero impact

---

### 9. **Test Cases Demonstrating Evidence-Only Filtering**

From `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/review/work_queue_cases.py`:

**Test: `test_evidence_only_finding_still_in_state()` (lines 761-769)**

- But **not in queue** (filtered out)

- All filtered from mechanical backlog

**Test: `test_impact_floor_filters_negligible_impact()` (lines 796-808)**

---

### 10. **Recent Commit: v0.9.0 "Evidence-Only Filtering"**

Commit `574d81d` (March 3, 2026) introduces:
- **Registry-driven `standalone_threshold`**: Detector metadata (not magic strings) controls which low-confidence findings are evidence-only
- **Preservation in state**: Evidence-only findings still contribute to dimension scores and are available for subjective review evidence
- **Impact floor addition**: Negligible-impact mechanical items dropped even with high confidence
- **Subjective policy unification**: Single `SubjectiveVisibility` dataclass replaces scattered visibility checks

---

### **Key Takeaways**

| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Classification** | `NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS` set determines subjective vs objective; `standalone_threshold` on detectors filters evidence-only |
| **Confidence** | HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW; lower than threshold = evidence-only (in state but not in queue) |
| **Review Flow** | `desloppify autofix review` prepares dimensions; batches via Codex/Claude cloud or manual import |
| **Routing** | Auto-fix → fixer, judgment/subjective → review/manual, evidence-only → state only |
| **Queue Gating** | Subjective items blocked by objective backlog unless marked `initial_review` or in explicit plan |
| **Impact Floor** | Mechanical findings < 0.05 estimated impact dropped (negligible score effect) |
| **State Integrity** | All findings kept in state; queue is filtered view for actionable work |

## Comprehensive Detector Registry and Dimension System Analysis

I've thoroughly explored the detector registry, dimension system, and fix/review flow in desloppify. Here's what I found:

### 1. DETECTOR REGISTRY (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/core/registry.py`)

**Core Structure:**
- `DetectorMeta` dataclass (frozen) defines all detector metadata:
  - `name`: Unique identifier (e.g., "unused", "smells", "orphaned")
  - `display`: Human-readable label for terminal output
  - `dimension`: Scoring dimension name (e.g., "Code quality", "File health")
  - `action_type`: One of `"auto_fix"`, `"refactor"`, `"reorganize"`, `"manual_fix"`
  - `guidance`: Narrative coaching text (shown in `desloppify scan` output)
  - `fixers`: Tuple of fixer names (e.g., `("unused-imports", "unused-vars")`)
  - `tool`: Optional tool name (e.g., `"move"` for reorganize detectors)
  - `structural`: Boolean (findings merge under "structural" in display)
  - `needs_judgment`: Boolean - whether findings need LLM design judgment
  - `standalone_threshold`: Optional confidence level (`"high"`, `"medium"`, `"low"`) - min confidence for standalone queue items

**Key Detectors:**

**Auto-fixable detectors:**
- `unused` (tier 3) - auto_fix with fixers: unused-imports, unused-vars, unused-params
- `logs` (tier 3) - auto_fix with fixer: debug-logs
- `smells` (tier 3) - auto_fix with fixers: dead-useeffect, empty-if-chain, **needs_judgment=True**, **standalone_threshold="medium"**

**Reorganize detectors (use `desloppify move`):**
- `orphaned`, `uncalled_functions`, `flat_dirs`, `naming`, `single_use`, `coupling`, `cycles`, `facade` - all mark **needs_judgment=True**

**Refactor detectors (complex changes):**
- `structural`, `props`, `react`, `dupes`, `patterns`, `dict_keys`, `test_coverage`, `signature` - many with **needs_judgment=True** and **standalone_threshold="medium"**

**Manual fix detectors:**
- `deprecated`, `stale_exclude`, `security`, `exports`, `global_mutable_config`, `private_imports`, `layer_violation` - all **manual_fix** action type

**43 detectors total** - ordered in `DISPLAY_ORDER` for consistent terminal rendering.

---

### 2. DIMENSIONS SYSTEM (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_scoring/policy/core.py`)

**Core Dimension Definition:**
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Dimension:
    name: str
    tier: int
    detectors: list[str]  # All detectors contributing to this dimension
```

**Mechanical (objective) Dimensions** - computed from detector findings:
1. **File health** (tier 3) - structural complexity indicators
2. **Code quality** (tier 3) - largest dimension; includes unused, logs, exports, smells, props, react, etc.
3. **Duplication** (tier 3) - dupes, boilerplate_duplication
4. **Test health** (tier 4) - test_coverage, subjective_review
5. **Security** (tier 4) - security, cycles

**Subjective Dimensions** - assessed via AI code review:
- High/Mid/Low elegance (22, 22, 12 weights respectively)
- Contracts (12), Type safety (12), Abstraction fit (8)
- Logic clarity (6), Structure nav (5), Error consistency (3), Naming quality (2), AI generated debt (1)
- Design coherence (10)

**Scoring Breakdown:**
- Mechanical dimensions: 40% of overall score (via MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION = 0.4)
- Subjective dimensions: 60% of overall score (via SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION = 0.6)
- Each dimension has: `score` (0-100), `strict` (excludes wontfix), `verified_strict` (excludes fixed/false_positive), `tier`, and per-detector breakdown

---

### 3. TIER SYSTEM (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/core/enums.py`)

```python
class Tier(enum.IntEnum):
    AUTO_FIX = 1
    QUICK_FIX = 2
    JUDGMENT = 3
    MAJOR_REFACTOR = 4
```

**Tier Assignment Rules** (in finding factories):
- **Tier 1 (AUTO_FIX)**: High-confidence, low-risk fixes
  - Unused imports (category == "imports")
  - Smell detectors with HIGH severity → Tier 2 actually
  
- **Tier 2 (QUICK_FIX)**: Medium confidence or higher complexity
  - Unused variables/params
  - Unused exports
  - Dupes (exact matches)
  - Dead functions (severity="high")
  
- **Tier 3 (JUDGMENT)**: Requires human judgment
  - Most default for structural/refactoring findings
  - Smell detectors: MEDIUM or LOW severity → Tier 3
  - Single-use files, cycles (<=3 files)
  
- **Tier 4 (MAJOR_REFACTOR)**: Large-scope changes
  - Test coverage
  - Longer cycles (>3 files)
  - Structural findings with 3+ complexity signals

---

### 4. CONFIDENCE SYSTEM (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/core/enums.py`)

```python
class Confidence(enum.StrEnum):
    HIGH = "high"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    LOW = "low"
```

**Confidence Assignment:**
- **HIGH**: Clear-cut detections (unused imports, exact duplicates, import cycles)
- **MEDIUM**: Heuristic-based findings (properties, smells, dupes with medium similarity)
- **LOW**: Low-confidence detections (near duplicates, some naming issues)

**Note:** `standalone_threshold` in registry gates visibility:
- Detectors with `standalone_threshold="medium"` only show findings that are MEDIUM or HIGH confidence in the work queue
- Evidence-only filtering: low-confidence findings below the threshold are excluded from standalone queue items

### 5. SMELL DETECTORS (TypeScript) - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/`

**Registered as single "smells" detector** in registry, but actually includes:

**Regex-based checks** (in `TS_SMELL_CHECKS`):
1. empty_catch - Empty catch blocks (HIGH severity)
2. any_type - Explicit `any` types (MEDIUM)
3. ts_ignore - @ts-ignore/@ts-expect-error (MEDIUM)
4. ts_nocheck - @ts-nocheck (HIGH)
5. non_null_assert - Non-null assertions ! (LOW)
6. hardcoded_color - Hardcoded color values (MEDIUM)
7. hardcoded_rgb - RGB/RGBA literals (MEDIUM)
8. magic_number - Magic numbers >1000 (LOW)
9. hardcoded_url - Hardcoded URLs (MEDIUM)
10. todo_fixme - TODO/FIXME/HACK comments (LOW)
11. debug_tag - Debug tags in logs (LOW)

**Multi-line/brace-tracked checks** (implemented in `_smell_helpers.py`):
1. **async_no_await** - Async functions without await
   - Algorithm: Track brace depth from `async` keyword, scan function body (up to 200 lines) for `await`
   - Maps to SMELL_TIER_MAP: (no explicit mapping, defaults to JUDGMENT=3)
   
2. **dead_useeffect** - useEffect with empty body
   - Algorithm: Two-pass paren/brace tracking to find useEffect call and arrow body
   - Strips comments and checks if body is empty
   - Severity: HIGH → Tier 2 (QUICK_FIX)
   
3. **empty_if_chain** - If/else chains where all branches are empty
   - Severity: HIGH → Tier 2
   
4. **console_error_no_throw** - console.error without throw/return
   - Severity: MEDIUM → Tier 3 (JUDGMENT)
   
5. **swallowed_error** - Catch blocks that only log (catch → console.error/warn/log)
   - Severity: MEDIUM → Tier 3

6. **monster_function** - Functions >150 LOC
7. **dead_function** - Functions with only empty/return-only bodies
8. **window_globals** - window object references
9. **nested_closures** - Excessive closure nesting

**All smells flow through:**
```
TS_SMELL_CHECKS detection → smell_counts dict → make_smell_findings()
→ Finding(detector="smells", tier=..., confidence=..., severity=...)
```

### 6. HOW FINDINGS FLOW THROUGH THE SYSTEM

**Detection Pipeline:**
```
Language Phase (e.g., detect_smells)
    ↓
Raw detector output (dict entries)
    ↓
Finding Factory (e.g., make_smell_findings)
    ↓
Finding (TypedDict with: id, detector, file, tier, confidence, status, etc.)
    ↓
State persistence (.desloppify/state.json → findings dict)
    ↓
Scoring (compute_health_score per dimension)
    ↓
Work Queue (ranking.py: item_sort_key) → plan.json
```

**Finding TypedDict** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_state/schema.py`):
```python
class Finding(TypedDict):
    id: str                    # detector::file::symbol
    detector: str              # "smells", "unused", etc.
    file: str                  # relative path
    tier: int                  # 1=AUTO_FIX, 2=QUICK_FIX, 3=JUDGMENT, 4=MAJOR_REFACTOR
    confidence: str            # "high", "medium", "low"
    summary: str               # Human description
    detail: dict[str, Any]     # Detector-specific data
    status: FindingStatus      # "open", "fixed", "wontfix", "false_positive", "auto_resolved"
    note: str | None
    first_seen: str (ISO timestamp)
    last_seen: str
    resolved_at: str | None
    reopen_count: int
    suppressed: bool (optional)
    zone: str (optional)       # "production", "test", "config", "generated", "script", "vendor"
    lang: str (optional)       # "typescript", "python", etc.
```

---

### 7. AUTO-FIX VS REVIEW DECISION LOGIC (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py` and `apply_flow.py`)

**Criteria for auto-fix readiness:**

1. **Detector must have `action_type == "auto_fix"`**
   - Registry examples: unused, logs, smells
   - Others (refactor, reorganize, manual_fix) require human judgment

2. **For smells specifically:**
   - `needs_judgment=True` in registry
   - BUT: available fixers: `"dead-useeffect"`, `"empty-if-chain"` enable auto-fix
   - So smells CAN auto-fix IF: detector supports the smell pattern AND fixers are available

3. **Confidence threshold filtering:**
   - If detector has `standalone_threshold`, filter out low-confidence findings
   - Example: `smells` has `standalone_threshold="medium"` → only MEDIUM/HIGH confidence in queue
   - LOW confidence smells don't appear in next/plan unless bundled with other findings

4. **Primary command assignment** (`primary_command_for_finding`):
   ```python
   if meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers:
       # Check if fixers are available for the language
       if fixer in supported_fixers:
           return f"desloppify autofix {fixer} --dry-run"
   else:
       return "desloppify plan done ..."  # Manual resolution command
   ```

5. **Review preparation flow** (`review_flow.py`):
   - `desloppify autofix review --prepare` generates dimension templates
   - Selects candidates where `status == "open"` AND not yet reviewed
   - Produces `.desloppify/query.json` with file content, prompts, dimension contexts
   - Feeds into external review runners (Codex, Claude cloud)

---

### 8. DETECTOR-TO-DIMENSION MAPPING

**Built dynamically from `DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES`:**

```
Detector → DetectorScoringPolicy(dimension="...", tier=...)
          ↓
          DIMENSIONS (computed list of Dimension objects)
          ↓
          dimension_scores in state (dict[str, DimensionScore])
```

**Example mappings:**
- `unused` → "Code quality" (tier 3)
- `smells` → "Code quality" (tier 3, file_based=True)
- `structural` → "File health" (tier 3)
- `security` → "Security" (tier 4, excluded_zones=production)
- `test_coverage` → "Test health" (tier 4, file_based=True, use_loc_weight=True)
- `cycles` → "Security" (tier 4)
- `review` → None (scored via subjective dimensions, not mechanical)

---

### 9. WORK QUEUE RANKING (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/ranking.py`)

**Sort key logic for findings:**
```python
def item_sort_key(item: dict) -> tuple:
    # Priority order: triage stages (-2) > workflow actions (-1) > clusters (0) > findings (1)
    # Within findings:
    #   - Subjective items before mechanical
    #   - High estimated_impact before low
    #   - Higher confidence (CONFIDENCE_ORDER: HIGH < MEDIUM < LOW as numbers)
    #   - Review items weighted by finding importance
    #   - Count of issues (higher count = higher priority)
```

**Evidence-only filtering** (lines 114-121):
```python
if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
    threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
    finding_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(finding.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
    if finding_rank > threshold_rank:
        continue  # Skip low-confidence findings below threshold
```

**Impact calculation** (`ranking.py:_compute_item_impact`):
```
impact = per_point_for_dimension × (100 - current_dimension_score)
# Items in low-scoring dimensions sort first
```

---

### 10. KEY RELATIONSHIPS

**Detector → DetectorMeta → Action Type → Fix Strategy:**
- `unused` (DetectorMeta.action_type="auto_fix") → `desloppify autofix unused-imports --dry-run`
- `smells` (action_type="auto_fix", needs_judgment=True) → `desloppify autofix dead-useeffect --dry-run`
- `naming` (action_type="reorganize", tool="move") → `desloppify move ...`
- `security` (action_type="manual_fix") → Review and manual changes

**Tier → Work Queue Priority:**
- Tier 1 (AUTO_FIX) items sorted highest
- Tier 4 (MAJOR_REFACTOR) items lowest unless high impact

**Confidence + Standalone Threshold → Visibility:**
- HIGH confidence: Always visible
- MEDIUM confidence: Visible if detector.standalone_threshold ≤ "medium"
- LOW confidence: Only visible if detector has no standalone_threshold, or bundled in clusters

**Dimension Tier → Score Weight:**
- Tier 3 dimension problems worth 3× the weight of Tier 1
- Tier 4 (test health, security) worth 4× the weight

This architecture ensures:
1. **Clarity**: Detectors are the single source of truth (registry.py)
2. **Composability**: Dimensions aggregate across detectors; scores propagate up
3. **Smart Filtering**: Confidence thresholds prevent low-signal noise from cluttering queues
4. **Judgment Safety**: `needs_judgment=True` detectors explicitly gate auto-fix and queue visibility
5. **Actionability**: Every finding has a clear primary command (autofix/move/plan done/review)

I need a detailed implementation plan for fixing three TypeScript smell detectors with high false positive rates, plus a holistic improvement to how questionable findings are routed.

## Context

The desloppify tool has a `smells` detector registered in `desloppify/core/registry.py` with:
- `standalone_threshold="medium"` — findings with confidence < medium become "evidence-only" (stay in state for scoring but don't appear in the work queue)
- `needs_judgment=True`
- Severity→confidence mapping: high/medium severity → "medium" confidence; low severity → "low" confidence

This means LOW severity smells are automatically evidence-only (don't clutter the queue). MEDIUM severity smells appear in the queue.

## Problem 1: `async_no_await` (70% FP rate)

**File:** `desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/_smell_helpers.py:79-123`

The detector uses raw substring matching `"await " in body_line` instead of using the existing `scan_code()` function to find `await` tokens in code positions. This means:
- Comments with "await" trigger false positives
- Strings with "await" trigger false negatives
- It has a hard 200-line cap that causes misses in long functions

**Fix:** Replace the raw substring check with proper token scanning using `scan_code()`. The brace-tracking loop already uses `scan_code()` — we just need to also detect `await` tokens within it (look for 'a' followed by 'w','a','i','t' not inside strings). OR more practically: after extracting the function body text between braces, use `scan_code()` to find `await` as a word token in non-string positions.

Actually the simplest fix: within the existing `for j in range(...)` loop that scans lines, instead of `"await " in body_line`, we should use scan_code on each body_line and look for `await` as a keyword token outside strings/comments. We already have `scan_code` imported. We can collect the non-string/non-comment text from each line and check for `\bawait\b` in that.

Also remove the 200-line cap — scan until braces close (the existing pattern in `_track_brace_body` scans up to 2000 lines).

## Problem 2: `console_error_no_throw` (85% FP rate)

**File:** `desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/_smell_effects.py:8-24`

The detector checks if `console.error` appears on a line and looks at the next 3 lines for `throw`/`return`. It has no context awareness.

**Fix:** Add exclusions for legitimate patterns:
1. Expand the lookahead check to also treat these as "handled": `toast(`, `normalizeAndPresentError`, `presentError`, `rethrow`
2. Skip if inside `componentDidCatch` method (check preceding lines for this method name)
3. Skip files matching logger/error utility patterns: filename contains `logger`, `errorPresentation`, `errorHandler`, `errorReporting`
4. Skip if inside dev-only blocks: if preceding lines contain `import.meta.env.DEV` or `process.env.NODE_ENV`

## Problem 3: `dead_function` (97% FP rate)

**File:** `desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/_smell_detectors.py:102-150`

The detector flags functions with empty/trivial bodies (empty, `return`, `return null`, `return undefined`). The name "dead_function" is misleading — it's really detecting stub functions. At 97% FP rate, almost all flagged functions are intentional stubs.

**Fix:**
1. Rename smell ID from `dead_function` to `stub_function`
2. Lower severity from "medium" to "low"
3. Update the label to "Stub/empty function body"
4. This automatically makes it evidence-only (below standalone_threshold="medium") — it still affects scoring but doesn't appear as a standalone queue item

## Problem 4: Holistic routing improvement

The existing `standalone_threshold` mechanism works well at the detector level. But within the `smells` detector, individual smell types have different reliability levels. The current system already handles this via severity→confidence→threshold:

- HIGH severity → medium confidence → in queue (tier 2)
- MEDIUM severity → medium confidence → in queue (tier 3) 
- LOW severity → low confidence → evidence-only

For smells that are inherently ambiguous and often intentional, lowering their severity to "low" routes them to evidence-only automatically. The dead_function→stub_function rename is the main one that needs this.

For `console_error_no_throw`, we fix the detection logic to reduce FPs rather than lowering severity, because genuine silent error swallowing IS worth catching.

For `async_no_await`, same — fix the logic, keep severity medium.

    46→                    cursor += 1
    47→                    continue
    48→                if re.match(r"(?:\}\s*)?else\s*\{\s*\}\s*$", next_stripped):
    49→                    cursor += 1
    50→                    continue
    51→                break
    52→            smell_counts["empty_if_chain"].append(
    53→                {
    54→                    "file": filepath,
    55→                    "line": chain_start + 1,
    56→                    "content": stripped[:100],
    57→                }
    58→            )
    59→            index = cursor
    60→            continue
    61→
    62→        if re.match(r"(?:else\s+)?if\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*$", stripped):
    63→            chain_start = index
    64→            chain_all_empty = True
    65→            cursor = index
    66→            while cursor < len(lines):
    67→                current = lines[cursor].strip()
    68→                if cursor == chain_start:
    69→                    if not re.match(r"(?:else\s+)?if\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*$", current):
    70→                        chain_all_empty = False
    71→                        break
    72→                elif re.match(r"\}\s*else\s+if\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*$", current):
    73→                    pass
    74→                elif re.match(r"\}\s*else\s*\{\s*$", current):
    75→                    pass
    76→                elif current == "}":
    77→                    lookahead = cursor + 1
    78→                    while lookahead < len(lines) and lines[lookahead].strip() == "":
    79→                        lookahead += 1
    80→                    if lookahead < len(lines) and re.match(
    81→                        r"else\s", lines[lookahead].strip()
    82→                    ):
    83→                        cursor = lookahead
    84→                        continue
    85→                    cursor += 1
    86→                    break
    87→                elif current == "":
    88→                    cursor += 1
    89→                    continue
    90→                else:
    91→                    chain_all_empty = False
    92→                    break
    93→                cursor += 1
    94→
    95→            if chain_all_empty and cursor > chain_start + 1:
    96→                smell_counts["empty_if_chain"].append(
    97→                    {
    98→                        "file": filepath,
    99→                        "line": chain_start + 1,
   100→                        "content": lines[chain_start].strip()[:100],
   101→                    }
   102→                )
   103→            index = max(index + 1, cursor)
   104→            continue
   105→
   106→        index += 1
   107→
   108→
   109→def detect_dead_useeffects(
   110→    filepath: str,
   111→    lines: list[str],
   112→    smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]],
   113→    *,
   114→    scan_code_fn,
   115→    strip_ts_comments_fn,
   116→) -> None:
   117→    """Find useEffect calls with empty or comment-only bodies."""
   118→    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
   119→        stripped = line.strip()
   120→        if not re.match(r"(?:React\.)?useEffect\s*\(\s*\(\s*\)\s*=>\s*\{", stripped):
   121→            continue
   122→
   123→        paren_depth = 0
   124→        end = None
   125→        for cursor in range(index, min(index + 30, len(lines))):
   126→            for _, ch, in_string in scan_code_fn(lines[cursor]):
   127→                if in_string:
   128→                    continue
   129→                if ch == "(":
   130→                    paren_depth += 1
   131→                elif ch == ")":
   132→                    paren_depth -= 1
   133→                    if paren_depth <= 0:
   134→                        end = cursor
   135→                        break
   136→            if end is not None:
   137→                break
   138→
   139→        if end is None:
   140→            continue
   141→
   142→        text = "\n".join(lines[index : end + 1])
   143→        arrow_pos = text.find("=>")
   144→        if arrow_pos == -1:
   145→            continue
   146→        brace_pos = text.find("{", arrow_pos)
   147→        if brace_pos == -1:
   148→            continue
   149→
   150→        depth = 0
   151→        body_end = None
   152→        for cursor, ch, in_string in scan_code_fn(text, brace_pos):
   153→            if in_string:
   154→                continue
   155→            if ch == "{":
   156→                depth += 1
   157→            elif ch == "}":
   158→                depth -= 1
   159→                if depth == 0:
   160→                    body_end = cursor
   161→                    break
   162→
   163→        if body_end is None:
   164→            continue
   165→
   166→        body = text[brace_pos + 1 : body_end]
   167→        if strip_ts_comments_fn(body).strip() == "":
   168→            smell_counts["dead_useeffect"].append(
   169→                {
   170→                    "file": filepath,
   171→                    "line": index + 1,
   172→                    "content": stripped[:100],
   173→                }
   174→            )
   175→
   176→
   177→def detect_swallowed_errors(
   178→    filepath: str,
   179→    content: str,
   180→    lines: list[str],
   181→    smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]],
   182→    *,
   183→    scan_code_fn,
   184→    strip_ts_comments_fn,
   185→) -> None:
   186→    """Find catch blocks whose only content is console.error/warn/log."""
   187→    catch_re = re.compile(r"catch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{")
   188→    for match in catch_re.finditer(content):
   189→        brace_start = match.end() - 1
   190→        depth = 0
   191→        body_end = None
   192→        for cursor, ch, in_string in scan_code_fn(
   193→            content,
   194→            brace_start,
   195→            min(brace_start + 500, len(content)),
   196→        ):
   197→            if in_string:
   198→                continue
   199→            if ch == "{":
   200→                depth += 1
   201→            elif ch == "}":
   202→                depth -= 1
   203→                if depth == 0:
   204→                    body_end = cursor
   205→                    break
   206→
   207→        if body_end is None:
   208→            continue
   209→
   210→        body = content[brace_start + 1 : body_end]
   211→        body_clean = strip_ts_comments_fn(body).strip()
   212→        if not body_clean:
   213→            continue
   214→
   215→        statements = [
   216→            stmt.strip().rstrip(";")
   217→            for stmt in re.split(r"[;\n]", body_clean)
   218→            if stmt.strip()
   219→        ]
   220→        if not statements:
   221→            continue
   222→
   223→        all_console = all(
   224→            re.match(r"console\.(error|warn|log)\s*\(", stmt) for stmt in statements
   225→        )
   226→        if all_console:
   227→            line_no = content[: match.start()].count("\n") + 1
   228→            smell_counts["swallowed_error"].append(
   229→                {
   230→                    "file": filepath,
   231→                    "line": line_no,
   232→                    "content": lines[line_no - 1].strip()[:100]
   233→                    if line_no <= len(lines)
   234→                    else "",
   235→                }
   236→            )
   237→
   238→
   239→def track_brace_body(
   240→    lines: list[str],
   241→    start_line: int,
   242→    *,
   243→    scan_code_fn,
   244→    max_scan: int = 2000,
   245→) -> int | None:
   246→    """Find closing brace that matches first opening brace from start_line."""
   247→    depth = 0
   248→    found_open = False
   249→    for line_idx in range(start_line, min(start_line + max_scan, len(lines))):
   250→        for _, ch, in_string in scan_code_fn(lines[line_idx]):
   251→            if in_string:
   252→                continue
   253→            if ch == "{":
   254→                depth += 1
   255→                found_open = True
   256→            elif ch == "}":
   257→                depth -= 1
   258→                if found_open and depth == 0:
   259→                    return line_idx
   260→    return None
   261→
   262→
   263→__all__ = [
   264→    "detect_dead_useeffects",
   265→    "detect_empty_if_chains",
   266→    "detect_error_no_throw",
   267→    "detect_swallowed_errors",
   268→    "track_brace_body",
   269→]
   270→

    30→def _find_function_start(line: str, next_lines: list[str]) -> str | None:
    31→    """Return function name for declarations/assignments, else None."""
    32→    stripped = line.strip()
    33→    if not stripped:
    34→        return None
    35→    if stripped.startswith(("interface ", "type ", "enum ", "class ")):
    36→        return None
    37→
    38→    declaration_match = re.match(
    39→        r"^(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(",
    40→        stripped,
    41→    )
    42→    if declaration_match:
    43→        return declaration_match.group(1)
    44→
    45→    assignment_match = re.match(
    46→        r"^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\b",
    47→        stripped,
    48→    )
    49→    if not assignment_match:
    50→        return None
    51→
    52→    combined = "\n".join(
    53→        [stripped] + [next_line.strip() for next_line in next_lines[:2]]
    54→    )
    55→    eq_pos = combined.find("=", assignment_match.end())
    56→    if eq_pos == -1:
    57→        return None
    58→    after_eq = combined[eq_pos + 1 :].lstrip()
    59→    if re.match(r"(?:async\s+)?\([^)]*\)\s*=>", after_eq):
    60→        return assignment_match.group(1)
    61→    if re.match(r"function\b", after_eq):
    62→        return assignment_match.group(1)
    63→    return None

   211→            if ch == "{":
   212→                depth += 1
   213→            elif ch == "}":
   214→                depth -= 1

   216→                    body_end = ci
   217→                    break
   218→
   219→        if body_end is None:
   220→            continue
   221→
   222→        body = content[brace_start + 1 : body_end]
   223→        # Check if body contains "return {" — a return with object literal
   224→        return_obj = re.search(r"\breturn\s*\{", body)
   225→        if not return_obj:

   227→
   228→        # Extract the returned object content
   229→        obj_start = body.find("{", return_obj.start())

   231→        obj_end = None

   233→            if in_s:

   236→                obj_depth += 1
   237→            elif ch == "}":

   240→                    obj_end = ci
   241→                    break

   243→        if obj_end is None:

   270→def _extract_function_body(
   271→    lines: list[str], start_line: int,
   272→) -> str | None:
   273→    """Extract the inner body text of a function starting at start_line.
   274→
   275→    Returns the text between the opening and closing braces, or None.
   276→    """
   277→    brace_line = _find_opening_brace_line(lines, start_line, window=5)
   278→    if brace_line is None:
   279→        return None
   280→    end_line = _track_brace_body(lines, brace_line, max_scan=2000)
   281→    if end_line is None:
   282→        return None
   283→    body_text = "\n".join(lines[brace_line : end_line + 1])
   284→    first_brace = body_text.find("{")
   285→    last_brace = body_text.rfind("}")
   286→    if first_brace == -1 or last_brace == -1 or first_brace >= last_brace:
   287→        return None
   288→    return body_text[first_brace + 1 : last_brace]

   291→def _count_pattern_in_body(body: str, pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> int:
   292→    """Count regex matches in body that aren't inside string literals."""
   293→    count = 0
   294→    for m in pattern.finditer(body):
   295→        pos = m.start()
   296→        line_start = body.rfind("\n", 0, pos) + 1
   297→        nl_pos = body.find("\n", pos)
   298→        line_text = body[line_start : nl_pos if nl_pos != -1 else len(body)]
   299→        if not _ts_match_is_in_string(line_text, pos - line_start):
   300→            count += 1
   301→    return count

   304→_FUNC_RE = re.compile(r"\bfunction\s*[\w(]")
   305→_ARROW_RE = re.compile(r"=>\s*\{")

   308→def _detect_nested_closures(
   309→    filepath: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   310→):
   311→    """Find functions with >= 3 nested closure definitions."""
   312→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   313→        name = _find_function_start(line, lines[i + 1 : i + 3])
   314→        if not name:
   315→            continue
   316→
   317→        body = _extract_function_body(lines, i)
   318→        if body is None:
   319→            continue
   320→
   321→        closure_count = (
   322→            _count_pattern_in_body(body, _FUNC_RE)
   323→            + _count_pattern_in_body(body, _ARROW_RE)
   324→        )
   325→        if closure_count >= 3:
   326→            smell_counts["nested_closure"].append(
   327→                {
   328→                    "file": filepath,

   330→                    "content": f"{name}() — {closure_count} nested closures",
   331→                }
   332→            )

   335→_TS_BRANCH_PATTERNS = (
   336→    r"\bif\s*\(",
   337→    r"\belse\s+if\s*\(",
   338→    r"\bcase\s+",
   339→    r"\bcatch\s*\(",
   340→    r"\bfor\s*\(",
   341→    r"\bwhile\s*\(",
   342→)

   345→def _compute_ts_cyclomatic_complexity(body: str) -> int:
   346→    """Compute cyclomatic complexity for a TypeScript function body string."""
   347→    stripped = _strip_ts_comments(body)
   348→    complexity = 1
   349→    for pattern in _TS_BRANCH_PATTERNS:
   350→        complexity += len(re.findall(pattern, stripped))
   351→    complexity += len(re.findall(r"&&", stripped))
   352→    complexity += len(re.findall(r"\|\|", stripped))
   353→    complexity += len(re.findall(r"\?(?!=)", stripped))
   354→    return complexity

   363→        if not name:
   364→            continue

   366→        body = _extract_function_body(lines, i)

   369→
   370→        complexity = _compute_ts_cyclomatic_complexity(body)

   381→def _detect_switch_no_default(

   383→):
   384→    """Flag switch statements that have no default case."""
   385→    switch_re = re.compile(r"\bswitch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{")
   386→    for m in switch_re.finditer(content):
   387→        brace_start = m.end() - 1
   388→        depth = 0
   389→        body_end = None
   390→        for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(
   391→            content,
   392→            brace_start,
   393→            min(brace_start + _MAX_SWITCH_BODY_SCAN, len(content)),
   394→        ):
   395→            if in_s:
   396→                continue
   397→            if ch == "{":
   398→                depth += 1
   399→            elif ch == "}":
   400→                depth -= 1
   401→                if depth == 0:
   402→                    body_end = ci
   403→                    break
   404→
   405→        if body_end is None:
   406→            continue
   407→
   408→        body = content[brace_start + 1 : body_end]
   409→        # Count case labels — only flag if there are actual cases
   410→        case_count = len(re.findall(r"\bcase\s+", body))
   411→        if case_count < 2:
   412→            continue
   413→
   414→        if re.search(r"\bdefault\s*:", body):
   415→            continue
   416→
   417→        line_no = content[: m.start()].count("\n") + 1
   418→        line_start = content.rfind("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
   419→        line_end = content.find("\n", m.start())
   420→        if line_end == -1:
   421→            line_end = len(content)
   422→        smell_counts["switch_no_default"].append(
   423→            {
   424→                "file": filepath,
   425→                "line": line_no,
   426→                "content": content[line_start:line_end].strip()[:100],
   427→            }
   428→        )
   429→
